title: Relative Clause Castle
description: Use who, whose, which and that. Join ideas and correct relative-pronoun mistakes.

questions.prompt: The woman ____ lives next door is a writer.
options: which
whose
when
who
questions.explanation: Who refers to a person and is the subject of lives.

questions.prompt: This is the boy ____ sister won the race.
options: who
which
that
whose
questions.explanation: Whose shows possession: the sister belongs to the boy's family.

questions.prompt: The watch, ____ belonged to my grandfather, is very old.
options: who
that
which
whose
questions.explanation: Which refers to a thing in a clause set off by commas; that is not used here.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that can replace who or which in a defining relative clause without showing possession.
options: whose
where
that
when
questions.explanation: That can introduce defining clauses about people or things; whose shows possession.

questions.prompt: I thanked the neighbour ____ helped us.
options: whose
when
who
which
questions.explanation: Who refers to the neighbour, a person who did the helping.

questions.prompt: We met a teacher ____ classroom contains old maps.
options: that
who
which
whose
questions.explanation: Whose links the teacher to the classroom.

questions.prompt: The necklace, ____ is made of silver, was a present.
options: which
who
whose
that
questions.explanation: A thing in a non-defining clause with commas takes which, not that.

questions.prompt: The pupils ____ names are on the list should wait here.
options: who
whose
which
that
questions.explanation: Whose shows that the names belong to the pupils.

questions.prompt: My aunt, ____ works in a library, enjoys reading.
options: that
who
which
whose
questions.explanation: Who refers to a person in a clause separated by commas.

questions.prompt: The album ____ has a red cover belongs to Dad. Choose a pronoun used for things.
options: which
whose
who
when
questions.explanation: Which refers to the album, a thing.

questions.prompt: Join using who: I know a girl. She speaks four languages.
options: I know a girl who speaks four languages.
I know a girl whose speaks four languages.
I know a girl which speaks four languages.
I know a girl who she speaks four languages.
questions.explanation: Who replaces she; do not repeat the subject pronoun.

questions.prompt: Join using whose: We met a boy. His father is a pilot.
options: We met a boy who his father is a pilot.
We met a boy whose his father is a pilot.
We met a boy whose father is a pilot.
We met a boy which father is a pilot.
questions.explanation: Whose replaces his to show the relationship between boy and father.

questions.prompt: Join using which: I found a box. It contains old letters.
options: I found a box which contains old letters.
I found a box whose contains old letters.
I found a box which it contains old letters.
I found a box who contains old letters.
questions.explanation: Which replaces it and refers to the box.

questions.prompt: Join using that: This is the book. It explains the custom.
options: This is the book whose explains the custom.
This is the book that explains the custom.
This is the book that explain the custom.
This is the book that it explains the custom.
questions.explanation: That replaces it; the singular book takes explains.

questions.prompt: Join using whose: I spoke to a woman. Her son collects stamps.
options: I spoke to a woman whose her son collects stamps.
I spoke to a woman who her son collects stamps.
I spoke to a woman which son collects stamps.
I spoke to a woman whose son collects stamps.
questions.explanation: Whose replaces her and links the woman to her son.

questions.prompt: Join using who: The man is our guide. He is carrying a torch.
options: The man whose is carrying a torch is our guide.
The man who is carrying a torch is our guide.
The man which is carrying a torch is our guide.
The man who he is carrying a torch is our guide.
questions.explanation: Who introduces information about the man without repeating he.

questions.prompt: Join using which: We saw a painting. It shows our town.
options: We saw a painting whose shows our town.
We saw a painting which shows our town.
We saw a painting who shows our town.
We saw a painting which it shows our town.
questions.explanation: Which refers to the painting and replaces it.

questions.prompt: Join using that: These are the letters. They tell our family story.
options: These are the letters that tells our family story.
These are the letters that tell our family story.
These are the letters whose tell our family story.
These are the letters that they tell our family story.
questions.explanation: That replaces they; plural letters takes tell.

questions.prompt: Correct the sentence: The girl which won the prize is my cousin.
options: The girl whose won the prize is my cousin.
The girl who she won the prize is my cousin.
The girl which she won the prize is my cousin.
The girl who won the prize is my cousin.
questions.explanation: Who refers to a person and replaces the incorrect which.

questions.prompt: Correct the sentence: This is the boy who mother is a doctor.
options: This is the boy whose mother is a doctor.
This is the boy that mother is a doctor.
This is the boy whose his mother is a doctor.
This is the boy which mother is a doctor.
questions.explanation: Use whose before mother to express possession.

questions.prompt: Correct the sentence: The clock who hangs in the hall is broken.
options: The clock which hangs in the hall is broken.
The clock which it hangs in the hall is broken.
The clock whose hangs in the hall is broken.
The clock who it hangs in the hall is broken.
questions.explanation: Which refers to a thing; do not add another subject it.

questions.prompt: Correct the sentence: We thanked the children who they helped us.
options: We thanked the children which they helped us.
We thanked the children who helped us.
We thanked the children who helps us.
We thanked the children whose helped us.
questions.explanation: Who already acts as the subject, so remove they.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The student whose project won is in my class.
The student which project won is in my class.
The student whose his project won is in my class.
The student who project won is in my class.
questions.explanation: Whose project shows which student the project belongs to.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The photographs whose show the village are on the table.
The photographs that shows the village are on the table.
The photographs who show the village are on the table.
The photographs that show the village are on the table.
questions.explanation: That refers to photographs; the plural subject takes show.

questions.prompt: In "I know the woman whose daughter is an artist", who is an artist?
options: The woman.
The speaker.
The daughter.
The woman's neighbour.
questions.explanation: Daughter is the subject of is an artist; whose links her to the woman.

questions.prompt: In "The guide who carried a lantern led the group", who carried the lantern?
options: The whole group.
The writer.
The guide.
A person outside the group.
questions.explanation: Who refers back to the guide.

questions.prompt: In "The ring which has a blue stone is mine", what has a blue stone?
options: The ring.
The owner.
The box.
The necklace.
questions.explanation: Which refers back to the ring.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that uses whose to show possession.
options: I read a book that describes Aqaba.
I met a girl whose uncle lives in Aqaba.
I met a girl who lives in Aqaba.
I saw a house which stands in Aqaba.
questions.explanation: Whose uncle connects the uncle to the girl.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly uses that for a person.
options: She is the teacher that she organised the trip.
She is the teacher that classroom is upstairs.
She is the teacher that her organised the trip.
She is the teacher that organised the trip.
questions.explanation: That may refer to a person in a defining relative clause and replaces the subject.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly uses that for a thing.
options: This is the medal that owner is my grandfather.
This is the medal that belong to my grandfather.
This is the medal that belongs to my grandfather.
This is the medal that it belongs to my grandfather.
questions.explanation: That refers to the medal; singular medal takes belongs.
